title: Pramila Jayapal's Resistance Lab -   Non- Violent Resistance Training
description:
The Resistance Lab 1.0- In-person, group training with Pramila Jayapal's staff by projected on Zoom

Sunday, June 1, 1:30 - 4:00 P.M.

The Resistance Lab is a series of trainings that are developed specifically for this moment. In this first lab, we look at how non-violent movements around the world have responded to leaders who seize power in authoritarian ways and the most effective tools and tactics to utilize in these moments. 

The Resistance Lab was developed with experts who have researched and studied democratic backsliding around the world as well as in the United States and the non-violent movements that have emerged to challenge those authoritarian leaders. We also draw from many toolkits for effective tactics and frameworks as well as from Pramila’s own background leading successful organizing movements for economic and social justice for two decades.

Our goals are to help people understand how democracies fall and the most effective resistance movements that have challenged authoritarians and dictators; to turn anger, fear and frustration into action in the short-term while also preparing for a coordinated resistance movement for the longer term; and to build community across the country that can help grow our movement. At the end of the day, we want to get people strike-ready and street-ready and make sure we protect our people, our freedoms and our democracy.

With Trump and his MAGA billionaires doubling down on their attacks on the economic livelihoods of people to thrive and on our democracy, we can’t afford to sit this moment out. This is about building real power together. And it starts with you.

title: Protect our trans siblings! No cuts to Medicaid and SNAP!
description:
Late Wednesday night the U.S. House of Representatives passed HR 1, a spending bill that would prohibit transgender people of any age from accessing gender-affirming care through Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP). This impacts 276,000+ transgender people currently enrolled in Medicaid. That’s 1 in 5 trans adults. 

The bill also contains the huge tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans while making the largest cuts to Medicaid and SNAP - ever. This legislation will rip healthcare and food from our families to line the pockets of the mega-rich. 

Now the bill moves to the Senate for a vote. It’s a bad bill period. But for the LGBTQIA+ community it is imperative that the discriminatory and dangerous language targeting trans and non-binary people is removed. By eliminating coverage for gender-affirming care, the bill not only undermines the health and dignity of transgender Americans but also sets a dangerous precedent for healthcare discrimination. 

Billionaires who will never need to rely on Medicaid want to cut it to give themselves tax breaks. We should make healthcare better for everyone, not take it away. Protecting access to comprehensive, inclusive healthcare must remain a national priority. 

Your Senators need to hear from you immediately that we won’t stand for any cuts to gender affirming care, Medicaid, and SNAP!

description:
Join us for Roadmap to Winning, a powerful gathering to celebrate how we beat back MAGA extremism—not with more money, but with more heart, more truth, and the will of the people. 

This event is more than a victory lap—it’s a strategy session for the future. We turned the tide in 2025. Now, we build the momentum to turn this first blue wave into a tidal wave in 2026. Learn from the organizers, leaders, and everyday heroes who made it happen—and how we do it again, bigger and bolder.

Together, we map the road ahead. Let’s keep fighting. Let’s keep winning.

**Featured Guest: Adam Kinzinger**

Adam Kinzinger is a former Republican congressman from Illinois and U.S. Air Force veteran known for his outspoken opposition to MAGA extremism. A key member of the January 6th Committee, he prioritized truth and accountability over party loyalty. After leaving Congress, he founded Country First to promote democracy and combat political division.

_**Panelists:**_

**Dr. John Biggan: HEB ISD Trustee**

Dr. John Biggan is a cognitive neuroscientist and data scientist who works in the child welfare system, using research and data to improve the lives of the children in this community, the state, and nationwide. A longtime Hurst resident and advocate for public education, he brings a research-driven approach to his role on the HEB ISD Board of Trustees, focusing on student success, teacher support, and fiscal responsibility.

**Vanessa Pacheco: Richardson ISD Trustee**

Vanessa Pacheco, single-member district 2; elected in June 2022. Mrs. Pacheco is the Chief Operations Officer for Carrolton Injury Law. She and her husband, Jorge, have a daughter who graduated from Berkner High School in 2020 and a son who graduated from Richardson High School in 2023.

**Amir Omar: Richardson Mayor**

Amir Omar is believed to be the first Muslim elected to political office in North Texas. Omar was elected to the Richardson City Council, Place 7 in May 2009, defeating incumbent Dennis Stewart by 51.54% to 48.46%. On May 3, 2025, Omar defeated incumbent Bob Dubey 54.4% to 41.6% in the mayoral race.

**Laney Hawes: Texas Freedom to Read Project and, Keller ISD Families for Public Education; Co-Founder**

Laney Hawes is the Co-Founder of the Texas Freedom to Read Project and the hyper local organization, Keller ISD Families for Public Education.  She's passionate about true grassroots activism, public education, and the freedom to read. Laney resides in North Fort Worth with her husband and four children.

**Adam Bazaldua: Dallas City Councilman**

Deputy Mayor Pro Tem Bazaldua is the youngest elected Council Member to the City of Dallas in its current form of government.Bazaldua is a dedicated father and husband who has been a chef and a teacher. title: Public Hearing for the Franklin County FY26 Budget
description:
The Franklin County Board of Commissioners meets on the first and third Monday of every month at 7:00 pm. We suggest you show up EARLY to grab a spot and sign up if you want to speak.

The next meeting is **June 2nd**. When it's shared, the agenda will be available [here](https://www.franklincountync.gov/government/board_of_county_commissioners/agenda_minutes.php).

They meet in Franklin Plaza Training Room​ at 279 South Bickett Boulevard​, Louisburg, NC 27549​. This is the same place we had our county convention and the same building as the senior center. It's located next to Tractor Supply in the Food Lion shopping center.


**_Message shared on Commissioner Mark Speed's Facebook page:_**

Y’all, I want to speak plain for a minute.
On June 2 at 7pm, the Board of Commissioners is holding a public hearing—and I need folks from every corner of Franklin County to show up and speak up.

If you’ve got something on your heart about how your tax dollars are being spent—whether it’s roads, schools, public safety, recreation or any other budget item—this is your time to be heard.

If you can’t be there in person, you can still make your voice count by leaving a comment online through the [Public Comment Portal](https://www.franklincountync.gov/county_services/budget___finance/budget_comment_portal.php?fbclid=IwY2xjawKd4jVleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETEwWk5vUUYyU044RDBnY1NWAR5EkfFt6rUV8X-Vvrz6ecavNfr48S6asvUjS7EeIEMklySJyuSceGpne1ZcgA_aem_em2jUWWdVkGyjO_zLRbxzg).

This county don’t run right without the people who live and work here being part of the conversation. Whether you wear boots or dress shoes, your voice matters the same.

June 2. 7pm. Let’s do right by Franklin County.

title: NO KINGS Flag Day Rally – Rock Springs
description:
Rock Springs - The home of 56 nationalities is celebrating our diversity on Flag Day!

This is OUR flag and we're taking it back! 

Bring ANY flag that represents you! 
The red, white, and blue, or the LGBTQ! 

Design a flag or bring many! 
Show your spirit!
And Fly, Fly, them high!

For years Trump supporters have draped themselves in the Stars and Stripes, wielding the American flag as a weapon to question our loyalty, our values, and our love for this country. They branded themselves as the sole arbiters of patriotism, painting us as weak, un-American, or worse. We knew it was a lie—a hollow performance rooted in division, not unity. But we let it slide, and that was our mistake. No more. The flag belongs to all of us, and it’s time we took it back.

The flag, once a beacon of collective strength, was weaponized. It became a prop for warmongering, a badge of arrogance, and a litmus test for loyalty. For years, they’ve flown it over their rallies, their tax cuts for the rich, their assaults on civil liberties—all while accusing us of hating the very country we’ve fought to improve. 

But now, Trump supporters, in their fervor for a single man, have traded the American flag for a new one: a blue banner emblazoned with “Trump,” worshiping him as if her were a king! They’ve replaced the symbol of nearly 250 years of struggle, sacrifice, and aspiration with the name of a convicted felon. They’ve chosen a cult of personality over the principles of a nation. And in doing so, they’ve given us an opening—a chance to reclaim what was always ours.

Let them keep their blue Trump flags. Let them wave them at their rallies with their silly red hats, plaster them on their trucks, and fly them in their yards. That’s not our flag. Our flag is the one that flew over Valley Forge, that was raised on Iwo Jima, that draped the coffins of those who died for freedom. Our flag is the one that stood defiant after 9/11, not as a symbol of who we are today, but of who we strive to be.

It’s time to fly the Stars and Stripes again—not with arrogance, but with purpose. Fly it in the face of an administration that thrives on division, lies, and the erosion of the very liberties we hold dear. Fly it as a hat tip to the generations who laid down their lives so we could protest, vote, and speak freely today. Fly it for the millions who’ve marched, bled, and died to protect this nation from the kind of tyranny we now face at home.

This isn’t about nostalgia or blind allegiance. It’s about defiance. It’s about reminding ourselves and the world that America was founded on rebellion against autocrats, on the radical idea that power belongs to the people. Let them have their Trump flags. We’ll take back the red, white, and blue. We’ll fly it as a symbol of resistance, of resilience, of a patriotism that doesn’t divide but unites. We’ll fly it for the America we believe in—an America that belongs to all of us, not just the loudest or the most hateful. And when we do, we’ll show the world that the soul of this nation isn’t found in one man or one party. It’s found in us, in our defiance, in our hope, and in the flag we raise together. The citizens of the United States of America worship no kings!
